team_news: As of 9 Oct 2026. Liverpool (Iraola presser, 9 Oct): OUT Alexander Isak (thigh, Sweden) and Cody Gakpo (ankle, Netherlands); Iraola: 'Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo will not play the game... They are not ready', and the injuries 'don't look like long-term'. On 7 Oct he had called both doubtful, so this supersedes that. Also OUT: Hugo Ekitike (Achilles, long-term), Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Federico Chiesa. Jeremy Jacquet has shaken off the hamstring strain that kept him out of France v Belgium and is projected to start at centre-back. No suspensions. Centre-forward options are Barcola, Victor Munoz, Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas; Iraola: 'Koumas has our trust... he has already shown he is ready to go.' Projected XI: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Munoz, Wirtz, Ngumoha; Barcola. Man City (Maresca presser, 9 Oct): Phil Foden SUSPENDED (final game of three-match ban from the derby red). Erling Haaland FIT after coming off as a precaution for Norway v Portugal; Maresca: 'He's good. He went to Marbella, two, three days off, played golf, recovery.' DOUBTS: Antoine Semenyo (ankle; some previews still expect him to start) and Nico O'Reilly (withdrew from England squad). Selection call between Cherki at No.10 or Bouaddi alongside Anderson. Off-field: City were found guilty on the Premier League financial charges this week and have appealed; Maresca says the players will not be distracted. No sanction affects this fixture. Sat 10 Oct update: no new Liverpool news since Iraola's Friday presser (Isak and Gakpo still out, Jacquet available); for City, reports say Semenyo was pictured in training this week and is expected to be available after his ankle problem, while there is still no update on O'Reilly's England injury (Gvardiol would cover left-back), and Maresca was not asked about either.
form_notes: City 5W from 5 (13-5), top on 15 pts, but margins narrow (1-0, 1-0, 2-1) apart from 4-1 at Palace and a 5-3 v Sunderland; conceded in 3 of 5. Liverpool unbeaten W2 D3 (7-4), 6th on 9 pts; draws 2-2 at Newcastle, 2-2 v Forest, 0-0 v Fulham; home record D2 (no home win yet). Iraola's Liverpool hard to beat; first Liverpool-City PL meeting without Klopp or Guardiola since 2015.
xg_notes: Per ats.io 5-game table: City xG 10.50 / xGA 7.18 (overperforming: 13 GF); Liverpool xG 8.34 / xGA 6.94 (7 GF). xG difference per game: City +0.66, Liverpool +0.28. Haaland scored in all 5 league games, 10 of 20 shots on target (RotoWire). Liverpool's xG likely depressed further by Isak/Gakpo/Ekitike absences.
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): Liverpool 1-2 Man City. RotoWire: 1-1. Another preview: 2-2. FreeTips: value on the draw at 11/4. ats.io: under 2.5. Jones Knows (Sky) column for this fixture not found.
reasoning: Opta (34.6/24.7/40.7) and the market (~35/26/39) both make City slight favourites, and City's xG difference (+0.66/game) is stronger than Liverpool's (+0.28). Liverpool losing Isak and Gakpo on top of Ekitike removes most of their centre-forward options, while City lose only Foden and have Haaland declared fit. I upweight the draw to 30% given the 32% season draw rate, Liverpool's three draws and that City's results are flattered by their xG. A rough Poisson (Liverpool ~1.3, City ~1.45 expected goals) makes 1-1 the single most likely score, but City win is the most likely result, and 1-2 fits Liverpool scoring in 4 of 5 and City conceding in 3 of 5.
risks: Semenyo or O'Reilly missing would weaken City a little. Liverpool's home crowd could make this a cagey 1-1 or 0-0. With all three natural centre-forwards out, Liverpool could struggle to create clear chances, or Barcola/Koumas could surprise a City side that has conceded in 3 of 5.
news_update_2026_10_10: Iraola's press conference on 9 Oct confirmed that Isak and Gakpo will not play, firming up what the previous team news already assumed, so it adds no new downside for Liverpool; it removes the upside scenario noted in the risks (Isak starting). Jacquet is fit, which is a small positive for the Liverpool back line, while Bradley, Leoni, Chiesa and Ekitike remain out. For City, Maresca confirmed Haaland is fit (as previously assumed) and Foden is suspended; Semenyo and O'Reilly are minor doubts. The prices (Football365 8/5, 11/4, 6/4) are close to the earlier Paddy Power quotes and still make City marginal favourites. None of this changes the picture behind my numbers, so my_probs stay at 32/30/38 and the 1-2 primary score is unchanged.
news_update_2026_10_10_evening: Little new. Liverpool: nothing beyond Iraola's Friday confirmation that Isak and Gakpo are out. City: Semenyo is reported to have trained this week and looks likely to be available (some predicted XIs still prefer Doku on the left); O'Reilly remains an unresolved doubt with no update since his England withdrawal. Odds: no fresher 1X2 found; prices seen are still 8/5 or 13/8, 11/4, 6/4 (Football365, Compare.bet), with Sporting Life's preview priced at 15:00 on 9 Oct, so the odds field is unchanged. Semenyo looking fit is a marginal plus for City, already partly assumed since previews expected him to start, and O'Reilly is a squad player with Gvardiol as cover, so my_probs stay at 32/30/38.

team_news: As of 9 Oct 2026. Coventry (Lampard presser, club report 8 Oct): Taiwo Awoniyi SUSPENDED (final game of ban for violent conduct v Brighton). Haji Wright OUT; Lampard: 'Haji won't be back until November at best' (quad injury from August; one Shields Gazette report says end of October). Josh Eccles (calf), Luke Woolfenden and Aurele Amenda OUT. RETURNING: Milan van Ewijk and Kaine Kesler-Hayden back in training. Brandon Thomas-Asante moved from the wing to lead the line. Predicted XI (3-4-2-1): Rushworth; Pinnock, Thomas, Mfuni; van Ewijk, Onyeka, Grimes, Dasilva; Rudoni, Tchaouna/Mason-Clark; Thomas-Asante. Newcastle (Jaissle; formal pre-Coventry press conference not yet held or reported as of 9 Oct, latest is the club injury update and Jaissle's comments this week): OUT Anthony Elanga (hamstring/thigh, return target around 7 Nov v Fulham); goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen OUT 'for a couple of months' after a training-ground injury (Hornicek has been starting). RETURNING: Joelinton in full training since Tuesday, minutes to be managed; Nico Gonzalez cleared concussion protocols and in full training; Dan Burn (ankle) and Amar Dedic expected back. DOUBT: Jacob Ramsey (thigh). Jaissle: 'For now, we hope three or four players are ready to be in the squad.' No Newcastle suspensions reported. Predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Gonzalez, Miley; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa. Sat 10 Oct update: Jaissle's pre-match press conference appears to have been held on Thursday 8 Oct (club site, VAVEL 8 Oct, Read Newcastle 9 Oct); the 'three or four players' comments above come from it, and no further Newcastle presser has been reported. Further 9 to 10 Oct coverage adds Jaissle saying some returnees could be in the squad 'but for sure not in the starting XI', with Joelinton and Burn tipped for the bench at best; Burn did not play in the behind-closed-doors friendly with Middlesbrough and is now reported as likely to miss (some list 17 Oct v Villa as his return); Ramsey (thigh) has not resumed team training (Craig Hope, Daily Mail) and faces a late check; Elanga still out; Dedic and Osula back in training and listed as minor doubts. Coventry: Van Ewijk on track to return if he comes through the final sessions (RotoWire); Kesler-Hayden back training but may need more time before making the matchday squad.
form_notes: Coventry (promoted) 18th, W1 L4, 1-10: lost 0-3 at Arsenal, 0-1 v Hull, 0-1 at City, 0-5 v Brighton, then won 1-0 at Forest in MW5. BTTS in none of their 5 games and only one goal scored, though four of the five opponents were strong. Newcastle 9th, W2 D2 L1, 9-9: 2-2 v Liverpool, 2-0 at Spurs, 2-2 v Bournemouth, 1-4 at Leeds, 2-1 v Hull. Four of their 5 games went over 2.5 goals, and they have one clean sheet.
xg_notes: OddAlerts xG table (5 games): Coventry xG 4.18 (0.84/game; 1 goal = heavy underperformance) and xGA 8.47; Newcastle xG 5.22 (1.04/game, while scoring 9 = overperformance) and xGA 9.92 (about 2/game, among the worst). On xG difference per game Newcastle (-0.94) are no better than Coventry (-0.86), and Coventry faced a much tougher schedule. Shots over the last 10 games (Gambling.com): Coventry 12.6 shots / 4.2 on target, Newcastle 12.7 / 4.5.
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): 1-1. RotoWire: 1-1. FreeSuperTips: 1-1. LiveScore: 1-1. Footballpredictions.com: 2-2. WhoScored: 0-2 (away win, under 2.5). Onside model: 1-2. Stats Insider: Newcastle 46.5%, best bet Under 2.5. Squawka: Newcastle win. Jones Knows not found.
reasoning: Opta (29.8/25.4/44.8) and the market (~28/26/46) favour Newcastle, but their underlying numbers are poor: about 1.0 xG for and 2.0 xGA per game, and their 9 goals well outstrip 5.2 xG. Coventry's xG is not much worse after a far harder schedule, so I trim Newcastle and push the draw to 30% (31% before the 10 Oct news update), close to the 32% season rate. I do not expect a heavy defeat for the promoted side. Coventry are missing both main forwards (Awoniyi suspended, Wright injured) and have scored once in five games, so a low-scoring Newcastle win is the most likely result. Rough expected goals of Coventry ~1.0 and Newcastle ~1.35 make 0-1 and 1-1 almost equally likely; 0-1 is the pick consistent with the most likely result.
risks: If the panel is short on draws, this is my preferred one to flip: 1-1 is near co-modal, and the consensus pick of Sutton, RotoWire and LiveScore. Coventry's xG suggests their finishing has to improve at some point, and Newcastle's leaky defence could give them the chance.
news_update_2026_10_10: Coventry's news is as expected: Awoniyi serves the last game of his ban and Lampard now says Wright will not be back until November at best, but Wright has been out since August, so his absence is already in Coventry's one-goal-in-five form; van Ewijk and Kesler-Hayden returning to training is a small help at wing-back. For Newcastle, Elanga is now confirmed out rather than doubtful, but that is outweighed by Joelinton (managed minutes), Nico Gonzalez, Burn and Dedic all returning to training, which deepens a squad that has been stretched. Jaouen's injury matters little because Hornicek has been starting. Newcastle's pre-match press conference had not been reported as of 9 Oct, so this rests on the club's injury update. The odds (12/5, 11/4, 11/10) have barely moved. Net, I move one point from the draw to Newcastle (28/31/41 to 28/30/42); Newcastle win stays the most likely result and 0-1 stays the primary score.
news_update_2026_10_10_evening: Modest change, mostly on Newcastle. Jaissle's pre-match press conference was in fact held on Thursday 8 Oct and its contents are already in the baseline; no Saturday presser has been reported. Newer reports are slightly less positive for Newcastle than the baseline: Burn now looks likely to miss rather than return, Ramsey has not rejoined team training, and Jaissle signalled that returnees such as Joelinton will not start. Dedic and Osula are training and should be available. For Coventry, Van Ewijk is on track and Kesler-Hayden is probably not ready for the squad. Odds: no fresher prices found (Compare.bet still 12/5, 11/4, 11/10), so the odds field is unchanged. my_probs stay at 28/30/42: Burn was not in the predicted XI, Joelinton's limited role was already assumed, and the net effect on the result is well under a percentage point.
